levels.label: Beginner
levels.description: Learners meeting a topic for the first time, regardless of age or institution.
typicalCharacteristics: Benefits from guided steps and explicit definitions.
Curriculum mapping is usually not applicable at this level.

levels.label: School
levels.description: School-stage learners (roughly classes 6-10 in the Indian system; equivalent stages vary by country).
typicalCharacteristics: Strong safety supervision required for wet chemistry.

levels.label: Higher secondary
levels.description: Pre-university learners (roughly classes 11-12 in the Indian system; A-level, IB or senior high-school equivalents elsewhere).
typicalCharacteristics: Working with quantitative relationships and laboratory technique.
Preparing for university study or applied science.
Curriculum mapping to boards such as CBSE is common at this level.

levels.label: Undergraduate
levels.description: University learners in foundation or intermediate chemistry study.
typicalCharacteristics: Comfortable with calculus-based or deeper quantitative treatment.
Independent laboratory work under institutional supervision.
Expects assumptions, error sources and model limitations to be explicit.

levels.label: Postgraduate
levels.description: Advanced university learners (master's stage and equivalent).
typicalCharacteristics: Critical reading of primary literature expected.

levels.label: Advanced / Research
levels.description: Researchers and advanced practitioners needing rigorous models, data and provenance.
typicalCharacteristics: Full model reports with validation evidence.
Precision, uncertainty and provenance are mandatory.
Content may exceed standard curriculum scope.
